# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 5 THE HOME COMING

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

Dr. David Carrow had dispatched his buggy and horse so they would be met, and the boy who was the driver sneaked off while grinning sympathetically, abandoning them to the joy of riding by themselves toward the house that was now theirs amidst the glowing dusk.
{: #nw-v04-c05-p0000 }

Nell never lost the memory of how beautiful the sight was that suddenly appeared before them as they crested the hill in back of the village. Although her new residence was not yet visible, Seven Gulls Harbor stretched out in front of her resembling a massive, gleaming mirror colored in rose and silver. Way below, she observed where it opened, situated between the sand dune bar to one side and a sheer, tall, severe cliff of red sandstone to the other. Past the bar, the ocean rested in the lingering light, tranquil and solemn. Tucked into the cove where the sand dunes joined the edge of the harbor, the small fishing village appeared to be a huge opal through the haze. Above them, the sky resembled a gem-encrusted cup spilling forth the twilight; the sea’s irresistible tang made the air crisp, and the entire scene was filled with the delicate nuances of a coastal evening. Along the darkening harbor banks lined with firs, several faint sails drifted by. From the tower of a small white church situated on the opposite side, a bell tolled; the sound floated softly and dreamily over the water, mixing with the ocean’s moan. Against the bright northern sky, the massive rotating beam located on the channel cliff shone warm and golden, acting as a flickering, trembling star of optimistic promise. Distant along the horizon, the smoke from a passing steamer formed a wrinkled gray ribbon.
{: #nw-v04-c05-p0001 }

“Oh, gorgeous, gorgeous,” whispered Nell. “Seven Gulls will be a place I love, Hugh. Which one is our house?”
{: #nw-v04-c05-p0002 }

“That strip of birch stretching from the small cove conceals it, so we are unable to see it yet. It sits approximately two miles away from Glen St. Agnes, with a further mile separating it from the light-house. Nell, our neighbors will be few. Just one house stands close to ours, and the identity of its occupants is unknown to me. Will loneliness affect you while I am absent?”
{: #nw-v04-c05-p0003 }

“Not when I am accompanied by such light and beauty. Hugh, who resides in that house?”
{: #nw-v04-c05-p0004 }

“I am uncertain. Does it appear—precisely—that the residents would be compatible souls, Nell?”
{: #nw-v04-c05-p0005 }

The residence was a grand, solid structure, coated in a green so intense that it made the surrounding countryside appear utterly washed out in comparison. An orchard lay in the rear, and a well-maintained lawn stretched out front, yet a particular starkness hung over the place. Its orderliness might have been to blame for this effect; every part of the property—the dwelling, outbuildings, fruit trees, garden plots, grass, and driveway—was unsparingly tidy.
{: #nw-v04-c05-p0006 }

“It appears unlikely that a person possessing such preferences in paint could prove to be VERY kindred,” admitted Nell, “except if it happened by chance—similar to our blue hall. At the very least, I am convinced that no children reside there. The neatness surpasses even that of the old Copp place located on the Tory road, an achievement I never anticipated seeing matched.”
{: #nw-v04-c05-p0007 }

No one had been encountered by them on the damp, red road curving beside the harbor edge. However, right prior to reaching the birch belt concealing their house, a girl was spotted by Nell, who was guiding a herd of snow-white geese atop a velvety green hill to the right. Large, dispersed firs were growing on it. Through their trunks, one caught sight of yellow harvest fields, flashes of golden sand-hills, and portions of blue sea. The girl possessed height and was wearing a light blue print dress. She moved with a particular spring in her step and an upright posture. Just as Nell and Hugh were passing, she and her geese emerged from the gate located at the hill's base. Placing her hand on the gate latch, she stood still, gazing intently at them with a look that scarcely reached interest, yet did not sink to curiosity. For a brief instant, Nell felt that a concealed trace of enmity was also present in it. Yet it was the girl’s attractiveness that caused Nell to let out a small gasp—an attractiveness so striking that anywhere it would have drawn notice. Though she wore no hat, thick braids of shiny hair, having the shade of ripe wheat, were wound around her head like a crown; her eyes possessed a blue, starry quality; her frame, inside its simple print dress, was splendid; and her lips matched the redness of the cluster of blood-red poppies attached to her belt.
{: #nw-v04-c05-p0008 }

“Nell inquired in a soft tone, “Who was that girl we just walked by, Hugh?””
{: #nw-v04-c05-p0009 }

“I failed to spot any girl,” remarked Hugh, whose gaze was fixed entirely on his bride.
{: #nw-v04-c05-p0010 }

“At that gate, she was standing—no, avoid looking behind us. We are still being watched by her. A face so beautiful has never been seen by me.”
{: #nw-v04-c05-p0011 }

“I fail to recall meeting any particularly attractive young women during my time in this place. A few charming girls reside up at the Glen, though I doubt they would qualify as truly beautiful.”
{: #nw-v04-c05-p0012 }

“She is, indeed. You could not have looked at her, otherwise you would recall her. No one is capable of forgetting her. A face like hers has never been seen by me, save in artwork. As for her hair! Browning’s phrases 'cord of gold’ and 'gorgeous snake’ were brought to my mind by it!”
{: #nw-v04-c05-p0013 }

“It is likely that she is a guest staying in Seven Gulls, perhaps a person visiting from the large summer hotel across the harbor.”
{: #nw-v04-c05-p0014 }

“Dressed in a white apron, she was herding geese.”
{: #nw-v04-c05-p0015 }

“To entertain herself, she could act that way. Observe, Nell—that is where we live.”
{: #nw-v04-c05-p0016 }

Nell gazed and temporarily pushed the girl possessing the magnificent, indignant eyes from her mind. Seeing her upcoming dwelling for the first time brought joy to her sight and soul—its appearance so strongly resembled a large, cream-colored seashell cast up on the bay's edge. The lines of lofty Lombardy poplars descending its path appeared in grand, violet outlines against the heavens. Situated behind it, protecting its garden from the excessively sharp gusts of ocean breezes, stood a hazy forest of firs, wherein the gales could create every sort of uncanny and lingering melody. As with any forest, it appeared to hold and embrace mysteries within its depths,—mysteries that yield their allure solely to those who go inside and search with endurance. Externally, deep emerald branches preserve them unviolated against inquisitive or unconcerned glances.
{: #nw-v04-c05-p0017 }

Past the bar, the wild dances of the night winds were starting, while lights gemmed the fishing hamlet on the other side of the harbor when Nell and Hugh came up the poplar lane in their buggy. A flickering, warm glow from the fire poured into the twilight as the door of the small house swung open. Hugh hoisted Nell down from the vehicle and guided her into the garden, passing through the small gate set between the firs with ruddy tips, and continuing along the neat, red path until they reached the step made of sandstone.
{: #nw-v04-c05-p0018 }

“Welcome home,” he murmured, and holding hands, they crossed the doorway of their house of dreams.
{: #nw-v04-c05-p0019 }
